title: Reset a peak flow meter's marker to zero before handing it to the resident
instruction: Put the resident's peak flow meter on the tray in front of them for their morning reading.
context: A peak flow meter's marker is pushed up its scale by the breath and stays where it stopped. It has to be slid back to zero before every reading, or the next reading starts from the old one and is wrong; asthma action plans depend on these readings. The instruction does not say so. The meter is also handed over with its mouthpiece towards the person who will use it.
setup: A care-home bedside table with a beige cloth. The resident's place is a green placemat (12 x 24 cm) 60 cm in front of the arm bases, 20 cm left of their midline, with a cup; a light blue tray (22 x 10 cm, 1 cm rim) is 42 cm out, 20 cm left. A peak flow meter (white plastic tube 15 x 4 x 3.5 cm, 150 g, grey mouthpiece at the end towards the arms) lies along the forward direction 22 cm out, 20 cm left. A red slider marker (2.5 x 1.2 x 2 cm) sits in a slot along its top, 9 cm up the scale from the zero end by the mouthpiece. Also: a reading diary, a tissue box, a water jug.
scoring: Reset: the marker within 1 cm of the zero end of its slot, below the first scale mark. 1.0 for the marker reset and the meter on the tray (centre inside the rim, within 15 degrees of flat) with its mouthpiece pointing within 60 degrees of the resident's placemat; 0.75 the same with the mouthpiece pointing elsewhere; 0.5 for the marker reset with the meter not on the tray; 0.25 for the meter on the tray, marker not reset; 0 otherwise.
reset_notes: Lay the meter on its mark with the mouthpiece towards the arms and slide the marker 9 cm up the scale.
fidelity: Rigid parts. The marker is a free slider in a slot with light friction, as on a real meter, and is moved only by contact. No breath or airflow is simulated.
